description: A team of new talents interested in space.
summary:
Pontes01 is a 2D pixel-art mission-design game where you command a spaceship with six crew members plus a commander, toward Pontes-01b (whose is in fact fictional), the nearest habitable planet found by Earth’s observatories. Before launch, you build the ship with 33 budget points (depending in your knowledge, up to 42 points) and 5 module slots, so every choice is a sacrifice. Then you manage resources, systems and people through random crises: meteor showers, radiation, fuel leaks, contaminated water, solar storms and the crew’s morale. Outcomes come from hidden d20 and d10 rolls, and you get clues instead of numbers. Crew members can die, and each loss removes a skill, unless commander takes it.

Real NASA science drives the decisions. Life-support numbers come from International Space Station references, such as 0.84 kg of O2/person/day and up to 98% of water recycling. Players compare real NASA exoplanet data, can choose any planet, even the wrong ones, and learn why each trip costs fuel, oxygen, food and days. A food system with a greenhouse, kitchen and rationing shows how astronauts really eat and grow food.

After landing, the game continues: players build the colony and light a beacon for the crew ships. It supports up to 7 players per spaceship (4 space ships) in the same activation code through peer-to-peer multiplayer, and it is available in Portuguese, English and Spanish.

The message: it is easier to keep Earth habitable than to inhabit another planet.
details:
Pontes01 (Bridges To The Space) is a 2D pixel-art space mission simulation game that runs in the browser. The player is the Commander of one of hundreds of ships launched toward Pontes-01b, a fictional habitable planet. Before launch, the player designs the mission with a limited budget (30 points and 5 module slots), chooses a route and leads six crew members. During the voyage, the player manages the ship’s eight systems, food, water, oxygen and morale through random crises such as meteor showers, leaks and solar storms. Outcomes come from hidden d20 and d10 rolls, so players get clues instead of numbers. Crew members can die, and each loss removes a skill. After landing, the game continues with building a colony. It also offers multiplayer (up to 6 players plus the Commander) in Portuguese, English and Spanish.

NASA open data shaped our mission definitions, real examples and how missions are planned. Life-support values follow ISS references (0.84 kg of oxygen per person per day, water recycling up to 98%), and players compare seven real exoplanets from the NASA Exoplanet Archive, with real facts and sources shown on the onboard computer. Pontes-01b is fictional and labeled as such.

Intended impact: raise awareness about pollution, rising global temperatures and the mismanagement of natural resources, and spark interest in science. The ending reveals that there is no planet B: on Earth, soil, rain and pollinators do for free what costs energy, time and lives on a ship.

Creativity: players learn by managing trade-offs and even by choosing the wrong planets, not through quizzes.

Tools: the game was generated with Claude Code (Anthropic) and is hosted on Vercel, with peer-to-peer multiplayer over WebRTC. The soundtrack was generated with Riffusion (AI). Claude helped edit the game script and helped with the translation and the voices. We did the ideas and brainstorming.
